page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2a server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an ARMv8 Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate modest performance characteristics. The instance achieves average single-core performance in stress-ng with a score of 1812.29 and single-threaded gzip compression at 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks show limitations, with a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 3594.57 and poor memory bandwidth performance, such as 139.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 26.99 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Passmark CPU and memory scores are also in the lower tiers, reflecting its entry-level ARM-based profile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 development and testing on Google Cloud Platform, leveraging dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. Given its performance profile, which includes weak database operations and poor static web serving throughput, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, ARM64 software compilation testing, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving.
